claims.text: Conventionally processed bulk refractory high-entropy alloys generally have coarse or moderately refined grain structures.
Severe plastic deformation followed by brief subcritical annealing will create a hierarchical structure of nanograins embedded within submicron grains in bulk RHEAs.
The hierarchical dual-scale structure will have a high density of grain boundaries.
High-density grain boundaries in the processed RHEA will act as sinks for irradiation-induced defects.
The increased grain-boundary area will suppress irradiation-induced defect clustering.
The hierarchical grain boundaries will facilitate dislocation movement and thereby improve ductility.
The thermomechanically processed RHEA will have significantly higher tensile strength than a conventionally processed RHEA.
The thermomechanically processed RHEA will have significantly higher yield strength than a conventionally processed RHEA.
The thermomechanically processed RHEA will have greater tensile ductility than a conventionally processed RHEA.
The thermomechanically processed RHEA will retain high-temperature stability despite its refined grain structure.
The thermomechanically processed RHEA will retain irradiation stability despite its refined grain structure.
Nanocrystalline RHEAs can exhibit high thermal stability, low irradiation-defect production or evolution, and no detectable irradiation-induced grain growth.
RHEAs are suitable candidates for high-temperature irradiation environments in the range of approximately 300–800 °C.
The proposed combination of strength, ductility, thermal stability, and irradiation stability should persist at moderate irradiation doses and operational temperatures.
Prolonged annealing may cause phase or microstructural instability that compromises performance.
Extreme irradiation levels may increase defect accumulation or irradiation hardening and compromise mechanical performance.
Ion irradiation provides only a partial proxy for reactor exposure, and neutron irradiation remains necessary for higher-confidence validation.
The magnitude of any mechanical improvement will depend on alloy composition and processing parameters.
